summary: Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and earned a PhD from UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, also studying under Noritoshi Aramaki and Shoryu Katsura. He served as professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Linguist and sinologist Changpei Luo studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held positions at Northwest University (~1924–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1934–1950).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002) under Masahiro Shimoda and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002) under Charles Hallisey and Morten Schlütter, having also studied under John D. Dunne.

Channa Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at Leiden University (2013–2019) under Jonathan A. Silk. Li was a postdoctoral researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2019) and a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Chao-heng Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. Affiliated with Academia Sinica (attested 2018), Liao also served as an adjunct researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene Makley, a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, received her PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999, studying under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She held a post as associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Linguist and Indologist Charles Albert Ferguson studied at the University of Pennsylvania (BA 1942). His career included posts at the Foreign Service Institute (1946–1955), Harvard (1955–1959), the Center for Applied Linguistics (Director, 1959–1967), and Stanford University (Professor, 1967–1988).

Philosopher Charles Alexander Moore earned his AB (~1926) and PhD (~1932) at Yale University and a DLitt from Visva-Bharati University (1967). He taught at Yale (1933–1936) and served as assistant professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967).

Charles Alfred Bell was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He was educated at Winchester College (~1884–1887) and New College, Oxford (~1887–1891), and served as a Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society (~1912–1945).

Charles Arthur Roe was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who studied at Merton College (~1860–1863). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1863–1898) and was Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University in 1895.
Charles Augustus Kincaid, who worked in Indology and history/archaeology, received his education at Sherborne School (~1884–1889) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1889–1891).

Charles B. Jones, a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, earned his PhD at the University of Virginia in 1996 under Paul Groner. He served as associate professor and associate dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

Linguist Charles Bally studied at the University of Geneva (1883) and Humboldt University of Berlin (dr.ph. ~1889), and studied under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1891–1913). He held posts at the University of Geneva (1893–1939) and Collège Calvin (1900–1913).
Charles Barbier de Meynard was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Julius Mohl. He held a post as a member of the Institut de France (attested 1894).
Charles Bowles was an Indology and linguistics scholar who served as Professor of Hindustani at Addiscombe Military Seminary (~1837–1861), where he succeeded John Shakespear.

Charles Bruce was an Indologist educated at Yale (1856) and the University of Tübingen (1861) under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the British Museum Library, served as unpaid Sanskrit professor at King's College London (1865–1869), and worked in the UK Government (1878–1904).

Charles Burnett, a scholar of history, archaeology, and philosophy, studied at the University of Cambridge (BA ~1972, doctorate ~1976). He held posts at the University of Sheffield (1982–1984) and the Warburg Institute, becoming professor there in 1999.
Charles Chapman was an Indologist who studied at Hoxton Academy and with traditional teacher Mahesha. He was a founder of The Asiatic Society.

Charles Cutler Torrey was a scholar in religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke (~1891–1892). He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and was a professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (attested 1998–2006) and was a National Humanities Center Fellow (2009–2010).
